title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026 · Gambler edition · By Richard J Diskin Jr

paragraphs: Monday night is final, so all 14 Week 10 games are graded, from Thursday night at MetLife Stadium to Monday night in Baltimore, with a Sunday morning stop in Munich. The Chargers tickets never trailed. The Over crowd was the one sweating: every Over in the room sat at 36 points with 14:56 left and needed a Baltimore touchdown to get home. Derrick Henry delivered it from 1 yard out at 10:23.

Graded against the opening lines, the Cover Writer went 9-5 against the spread and 3-11 on the over/under. Graded against the closing lines, the Cover Writer went 9-5 against the spread and 7-7 on the over/under.

Every side is graded on the team picked and every over/under on the Over or Under called, once against the opening line and once against the closing line. A push counts as neither a hit nor a miss, overtime points count, and picks are graded as they stood at kickoff. Monday's game-day line refresh moved every Chargers-Ravens side ticket from 5.5 to 4.5 and added Follow The Money on the Chargers, and nothing changed after that. Monday night gets the full ride. The rest of the week gets a quick lap, with the plays that swung the tickets.

Opening line: Ravens −3.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: Ravens −4.5, over/under 39.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Chargers and the Over, projecting Ravens 23, Chargers 19. Final: Chargers 23, Ravens 20. The Chargers won by 3, and the teams scored 43 points.

The Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches took the Chargers +4.5. The Formula and Letdown Watch laid the 4.5 with Baltimore. Every over/under pick in the room was the Over 38.5, and Follow The Money stayed off the over/under. Lamar Jackson was on injured reserve, so Jacoby Brissett started for the Ravens. The over/under fell 8 points from the open to the close, so the Over was a very different ticket depending on the day it was bought.

The Chargers tickets were cashing from the first drive. On third-and-6 at the Baltimore 22, Justin Herbert scrambled up the middle for a 22-yard touchdown at 10:39 of the first. Later in the quarter Los Angeles challenged an incomplete deep ball to Tre' Harris, replay turned it into a 31-yard catch at the Baltimore 26, and Cameron Dicker hit from 38. Chargers 10, Ravens 0.

Derrick Henry scored from 2 yards at 12:33 of the second. Chargers 10, Ravens 7. Two snaps into Baltimore's next drive, Del'Shawn Phillips intercepted Brissett, and the Chargers kept the ball for 13 plays and 7:35. Omarion Hampton converted a fourth-and-1 at the Baltimore 39, a 15-yard unnecessary roughness flag on the Chargers pushed them right back, and they kept going anyway. Herbert scrambled to the 1 on third-and-goal, and Hampton went in on fourth-and-goal with 1:56 left in the half. Chargers 17, Ravens 7.

Baltimore answered with a 72-yard drive that had three flags on it and ended at the Chargers 8 with 3 seconds left, and Riley Patterson kicked a 26-yarder as the half ended. Chargers 17, Ravens 10 at the half, 27 points. The Chargers +4.5 was covering by 11.5, and the Over 38.5 on the card needed 12 more points in the second half.

The third quarter went field goal for field goal. Dalvin Tomlinson sacked Brissett at the 6 on third-and-3, the punt return set the Chargers up at the Baltimore 37, and Dicker hit from 34 at 9:03. Chargers 20, Ravens 10, 30 points. Baltimore stalled at the Chargers 17 after a no-gain run and two incompletions, and Patterson hit from 36 at 3:36. Chargers 20, Ravens 13, 33 points.

Then came the flag that kept the Over alive. On the first snap of the next Chargers drive, Herbert threw incomplete and Mike Green was called for roughing the passer, 15 yards. Hampton ran for 16 and 13 on the next two snaps, the drive stalled at the 17, and Dicker's 35-yarder at 14:56 of the fourth made it Chargers 23, Ravens 13, 36 points. The Over 38.5 needed 3 more points and the closing 39.5 needed 4.

Baltimore went 71 yards in 10 plays. Brissett hit Mark Andrews for 13 yards to the 4, and Henry scored from 1 yard on third-and-goal at 10:23. Chargers 23, Ravens 20, 43 points. Every Over ticket on the card cashed right there, by 4.5 at the card's 38.5 and by 3.5 at the closing 39.5. Anybody holding the Over at the opening 47.5 needed 5 more points and never saw them.

That left The Formula and Letdown Watch, the only Ravens tickets in the room, needing Baltimore to win by 5. The Ravens punted on fourth-and-9 from their own 42 at 4:11. They got one more look at 2:24, and on second-and-10 Brissett hit Zay Flowers for 15 yards, Tarheeb Still punched the ball out, and Elijah Molden recovered at the Chargers 46. Even a Baltimore touchdown on that drive would have won the game by 4, still half a point short of the 4.5. The Chargers ran it down, took a delay of game on fourth-and-2 with 18 seconds left, and punted for a touchback. Brissett's last throw, deep for Ja'Kobi Lane, fell incomplete.

The damage report. The Chargers won by 3, so the Chargers +4.5 covered by 7.5 and the Ravens −4.5 missed by 7.5, and at the opening Ravens −3.5 the margin was 6.5 both ways. Hampton ran 22 times for 105 yards, and Herbert threw for 129 and ran for 51. Brissett threw for 340 yards with no touchdowns, and Baltimore ran 15 times for 16 yards. Henry carried 10 times for 10 yards, and two of those carries were the Ravens' only touchdowns. Next Man Up projected Ravens 22, Chargers 21, the closest call in the room on the final margin, and In The Trenches projected 39 points and took the Over 38.5.
Missed at both numbers: The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Ravens, missed by 6.5 points at the opening Ravens −3.5 and missed by 7.5 points at the closing Ravens −4.5.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 4.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 3.5 points at the closing 39.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on the Chargers, covered by 6.5 points at the opening Chargers +3.5 and covered by 7.5 points at the closing Chargers +4.5.
Follow The Money had no over/under pick.

Opening line: Bengals −3.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: Bengals −4.5, over/under 49.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Steelers and the Under, projecting Bengals 25, Steelers 22. Final: Steelers 18, Bengals 38. The Bengals won by 20, and the teams scored 56 points.

The Formula was alone on the Bengals, and the side was settled at halftime, Bengals 24, Steelers 3. The Under 49.5 was the sweat. Samaje Perine's 1-yard touchdown at 10:08 of the fourth made it Bengals 38, Steelers 11, 49 points, half a point to spare. Then Kris Jenkins Jr. was flagged for roughing the passer at 8:18, and Aaron Rodgers hit Pat Freiermuth for a 27-yard touchdown at 7:19. Bengals 38, Steelers 18, 56 points. Follow The Money's Over was the only over/under winner, and In The Trenches had switched from the Over to the Under on Sunday morning.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Steelers, missed by 16.5 points at the opening Steelers +3.5 and missed by 15.5 points at the closing Steelers +4.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, went over by 8.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 6.5 points at the closing 49.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Formula on the Bengals, covered by 16.5 points at the opening Bengals −3.5 and covered by 15.5 points at the closing Bengals −4.5; Follow The Money on the Over, went over by 8.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 6.5 points at the closing 49.5.
Follow The Money sat out the side.

Opening line: Cowboys −1.5, over/under 52.5. Closing line: 49ers −3.5, over/under 55.5. The Cover Writer's card had the 49ers and the Under, projecting 49ers 30, Cowboys 23. Final: 49ers 46, Cowboys 40. The 49ers won by 6, and the teams scored 86 points.

Everybody but In The Trenches had the Under 55.5, and it was dead at 11:26 of the fourth, when Christian McCaffrey's 16-yard touchdown run made it 49ers 38, Cowboys 19, 57 points. The side went to the last snap. CeeDee Lamb caught a 1-yard touchdown at 0:43 and Dak Prescott ran in the two-point try. 49ers 46, Cowboys 40, so the 49ers −4.5 was covering by 1.5 and a Dallas field goal would have flipped it. Deebo Samuel Sr. fielded the onside kick, and the game ended on a string of laterals and a fumble recovered by Marques Sigle. In The Trenches' Over cashed by 30.5, and Next Man Up's Cowboys +4.5 missed by 1.5.

Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up on the Cowboys, missed by 7.5 points at the opening Cowboys −1.5 and missed by 2.5 points at the closing Cowboys +3.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under, went over by 33.5 points at the opening 52.5 and went over by 30.5 points at the closing 55.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the 49ers, covered by 7.5 points at the opening 49ers +1.5 and covered by 2.5 points at the closing 49ers −3.5; In The Trenches on the Over, went over by 33.5 points at the opening 52.5 and went over by 30.5 points at the closing 55.5.
Follow The Money stayed off the side and the over/under.

Opening line: Seahawks −7, over/under 43.5. Closing line: Seahawks −6.5, over/under 40.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Seahawks and the Over, projecting Seahawks 26, Raiders 19. Final: Seahawks 21, Raiders 13. The Seahawks won by 8, and the teams scored 34 points.

Five pickers had the Over 40.5, and it died on two empty Seattle trips in the fourth. Up 21-10, Seattle drove 14 plays and lost a sack-fumble at the Raiders' 12 at 12:17, recovered by Nakobe Dean, and Jason Myers missed a 44-yarder wide right at 7:05. Matt Gay's 43-yarder on fourth-and-20 at 2:04 made it Seahawks 21, Raiders 13, 34 points, and the Raiders +6.5 needed the ball back. A 15-yard scramble on second-and-11 at 1:55 ended that, and the Seahawks −6.5 covered by 1.5 through three kneel-downs. Next Man Up and In The Trenches had the Seahawks −3.5 and the Under 43.5 before Sunday's refresh, switched to the Raiders and the Over, and lost both. The original pair would have cashed both.

Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Raiders, missed by 1 point at the opening Raiders +7 and missed by 1.5 points at the closing Raiders +6.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 9.5 points at the opening 43.5 and fell short by 6.5 points at the closing 40.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on the Seahawks, covered by 1 point at the opening Seahawks −7 and covered by 1.5 points at the closing Seahawks −6.5; Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 9.5 points at the opening 43.5 and stayed under by 6.5 points at the closing 40.5.

Opening line: Rams −10.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: Rams −10, over/under 38.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Cardinals and the Over, projecting Rams 27, Cardinals 19. Final: Rams 34, Cardinals 6. The Rams won by 28, and the teams scored 40 points.

Every picker with a side had the Cardinals +9.5, and that was over at 5:55 of the third when Davis Allen's 19-yard touchdown made it Rams 31, Cardinals 6. The over/under fell 9 points from the open to the close, and every Over 38.5 sat at 37 points until Darius Robinson jumped for a neutral zone infraction on fourth-and-1 at the Arizona 35. Brandon McManus finished that drive with a 43-yarder at 14:55 of the fourth. Rams 34, Cardinals 6, 40 points. The Over 38.5 cashed by 1.5, and the same kick beat Follow The Money's Under by 1.5. The Rams kept the ball for 17 plays to end it, and the opening 47.5 never came into view.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Cardinals, missed by 17.5 points at the opening Cardinals +10.5 and missed by 18 points at the closing Cardinals +10.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 7.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 1.5 points at the closing 38.5; Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 7.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 1.5 points at the closing 38.5.
Follow The Money had nothing on the side.

Opening line: Chiefs −4.5, over/under 45.5. Closing line: Chiefs −3.5, over/under 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Chiefs and the Under, projecting Chiefs 24, Falcons 20. Final: Chiefs 35, Falcons 13. The Chiefs won by 22, and the teams scored 48 points.

Kansas City won 35-13 in Atlanta, and Patrick Mahomes threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns. His 18-yard touchdown throw to Josh Downs made it 14-3 with 18 seconds left in the half. The total sat at 41 after Jake Moody's 38-yard field goal at 6:45 of the fourth. On third-and-1 at 4:18, Mahomes found Andrew Armstrong for a 43-yard touchdown. That made 48 points: the Under 47.5 lost by half a point, and Follow The Money's Over won by the same half point.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, went over by 2.5 points at the opening 45.5 and went over by half a point at the closing 47.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Chiefs, covered by 17.5 points at the opening Chiefs −4.5 and covered by 18.5 points at the closing Chiefs −3.5; Follow The Money on the Over, went over by 2.5 points at the opening 45.5 and went over by half a point at the closing 47.5.
Follow The Money had no side pick.

Opening line: Texans −4.5, over/under 38.5. Closing line: Texans −3.5, over/under 41. The Cover Writer's card had the Browns and the Over, projecting Texans 23, Browns 19. Final: Texans 24, Browns 27. The Browns won by 3, and the teams scored 51 points.

The flags ran this one. With Cleveland up 20-17, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren intercepted C.J. Stroud, a 37-yard pass interference call on Myles Harden wiped it out, and Stroud hit Dalton Schultz for an 11-yard touchdown at 9:17. Texans 24, Browns 20, and the Browns +4.5 was covering by half a point. Calen Bullock intercepted Deshaun Watson at 5:19, a 15-yard unnecessary roughness flag on Kamari Lassiter moved Cleveland into Houston territory, and Quinshon Judkins ran in from the 5 with 53 seconds left. Browns 27, Texans 24. Houston's fourth-and-10 conversion came back on a holding call, and the Browns +4.5 covered by 7.5. The Over had cashed back at 9:17, and In The Trenches, which left the Over for the Under on Sunday morning, missed by 10.5.

Missed at both numbers: The Formula and In The Trenches on the Texans, missed by 7.5 points at the opening Texans −4.5 and missed by 6.5 points at the closing Texans −3.5; In The Trenches on the Under, went over by 12.5 points at the opening 38.5 and went over by 10 points at the closing 41.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Browns, covered by 7.5 points at the opening Browns +4.5 and covered by 6.5 points at the closing Browns +3.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on the Over, went over by 12.5 points at the opening 38.5 and went over by 10 points at the closing 41.
Follow The Money kept its money off the side.

Opening line: Packers −4.5, over/under 45.5. Closing line: Packers −2.5, over/under 42.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Vikings and the Under, projecting Packers 20, Vikings 18. Final: Vikings 30, Packers 10. The Vikings won by 20, and the teams scored 40 points.

The Formula was alone on the Packers −2.5, and the Vikings led 17-0 at the half. The Under 42.5 was the sweat. Minnesota got to fourth-and-goal at the 2 with 37 points on the board and kicked a 20-yard field goal at 3:56. A touchdown there makes it 44 and beats the Under. Will Reichard's chip shot left it at 40, the Under cashed by 2.5 for five pickers, and Follow The Money's Over came up 2.5 short. The Vikings +2.5 covered by 22.5.

Missed at both numbers: The Formula on the Packers, missed by 24.5 points at the opening Packers −4.5 and missed by 22.5 points at the closing Packers −2.5; Follow The Money on the Over, fell short by 5.5 points at the opening 45.5 and fell short by 2.5 points at the closing 42.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on the Vikings, covered by 24.5 points at the opening Vikings +4.5 and covered by 22.5 points at the closing Vikings +2.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, stayed under by 5.5 points at the opening 45.5 and stayed under by 2.5 points at the closing 42.5.

Opening line: Jaguars −2.5, over/under 45.5. Closing line: Jaguars −11, over/under 45.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Titans and the Under, projecting Jaguars 27, Titans 17. Final: Jaguars 40, Titans 23. The Jaguars won by 17, and the teams scored 63 points.

This line moved 8.5 points toward Jacksonville from the open to the close. The card's Under 46.5 survived Trevor Lawrence's 25-yard touchdown pass to Josh Cameron at 9:44 of the fourth by half a point, Jaguars 30, Titans 16, 46 points, and died one drive later on Tony Pollard's 32-yard touchdown catch at 8:21. Then the side got tense. Cam Little's 40-yarder at 4:31 made it Jaguars 33, Titans 23, and the Titans +10.5 was covering by half a point. Pollard was stopped on fourth-and-1 at 3:11, and Bhayshul Tuten ran in from 6 yards at 1:10. Jaguars 40, Titans 23. The Titans +10.5 missed by 6.5, The Formula and Letdown Watch cashed the Jaguars −10.5, and In The Trenches' Over cashed by 16.5.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Titans, missed by 14.5 points at the opening Titans +2.5 and missed by 6 points at the closing Titans +11; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under, went over by 17.5 points at the opening 45.5 and went over by 17.5 points at the closing 45.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Jaguars, covered by 14.5 points at the opening Jaguars −2.5 and covered by 6 points at the closing Jaguars −11; In The Trenches on the Over, went over by 17.5 points at the opening 45.5 and went over by 17.5 points at the closing 45.5.
Follow The Money had no side or over/under pick.

Opening line: Colts −6.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: Colts −5, over/under 37.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Dolphins and the Over, projecting Colts 24, Dolphins 20. Final: Dolphins 22, Colts 24. The Colts won by 2, and the teams scored 46 points.

Three pickers left the Colts −2.5 for the Dolphins +4.5 on Sunday morning, and the switch paid. Spencer Shrader's 51-yarder made it Colts 24, Dolphins 16, 40 points, and the Over 37.5 on the card was home. The opening 47.5 was another story, and it died on three Miami misses: Zane Gonzalez's missed extra point after Chris Johnson's 59-yard pick-six, the incomplete two-point pass after Kyle McCord's 3-yard touchdown run at 14:56 of the fourth, and Gonzalez's miss from 51 at 9:54. Those 6 points that never happened left the game at 46, 1.5 short of the open. The Colts won by 2, the Dolphins +4.5 covered by 2.5, and Next Man Up and Follow The Money lost the Colts −4.5 by 2.5.
Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up and Follow The Money on the Colts, missed by 4.5 points at the opening Colts −6.5 and missed by 3 points at the closing Colts −5.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 1.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 8.5 points at the closing 37.5; Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 1.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 8.5 points at the closing 37.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Dolphins, covered by 4.5 points at the opening Dolphins +6.5 and covered by 3 points at the closing Dolphins +5.

Opening line: Saints −1.5, over/under 43.5. Closing line: Panthers −1.5, over/under 48.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Panthers and the Over, projecting Panthers 25, Saints 24. Final: Panthers 20, Saints 17. The Panthers won by 3, and the teams scored 37 points.

The favorite flipped between the open and the close, so the Panthers ticket was +1.5 or −1.5 depending on when it was bought. Charlie Smyth's 55-yarder at 0:41 tied it 17-17, and the Panthers at the closing −1.5 were losing by 1.5. Carolina had 41 seconds. Kool-Aid McKinstry was flagged for 30 yards of pass interference, and Ryan Fitzgerald hit a 54-yarder as time ran out. Panthers 20, Saints 17. The Panthers covered at both numbers, Letdown Watch's Saints −1.5 missed by 4.5, and 37 points paid the Under for Next Man Up and Letdown Watch by 11.5 at the close.

Missed at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Saints, missed by 4.5 points at the opening Saints −1.5 and missed by 1.5 points at the closing Saints +1.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 6.5 points at the opening 43.5 and fell short by 11.5 points at the closing 48.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Panthers, covered by 4.5 points at the opening Panthers +1.5 and covered by 1.5 points at the closing Panthers −1.5; Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under, stayed under by 6.5 points at the opening 43.5 and stayed under by 11.5 points at the closing 48.5.
Follow The Money sat out the side and the over/under.

Opening line: Bills −7, over/under 46.5. Closing line: Bills −8, over/under 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Jets and the Under, projecting Bills 28, Jets 21. Final: Bills 31, Jets 12. The Bills won by 19, and the teams scored 43 points.

Everybody but Letdown Watch had the Jets +8.5, and the Jets were within 17-12 with 4:21 left in the third. Josh Allen hit DJ Moore for a 45-yard touchdown 39 seconds later. Then the Jets drove to the Buffalo 23, Garrett Wilson fumbled at the 19, Kaleb Elarms-Orr recovered at 4:59, and James Cook III ran 74 yards for a touchdown on the next play. Bills 31, Jets 12, 43 points. The Jets +8.5 missed by 10.5, Letdown Watch's Bills −8.5 covered, and all five Under tickets survived a last Jets drive that died on fourth-and-11 at 1:54.
Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Jets, missed by 12 points at the opening Jets +7 and missed by 11 points at the closing Jets +8.

Called it at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Bills, covered by 12 points at the opening Bills −7 and covered by 11 points at the closing Bills −8; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, stayed under by 3.5 points at the opening 46.5 and stayed under by 7.5 points at the closing 50.5.
Follow The Money had nothing on the side and the over/under.

Opening line: Lions −1.5, over/under 48.5. Closing line: Lions −2.5, over/under 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Patriots and the Over, projecting Patriots 26, Lions 25. Final: Patriots 10, Lions 35. The Lions won by 25, and the teams scored 45 points.

Detroit won 35-10 in Munich. Drake Maye took a third-down sack on the opening drive, and Tommy DeVito played the rest of the way. Jared Goff threw for 303 yards and three touchdowns, two to Amon-Ra St. Brown. Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and two scores. His 28-yard touchdown at 8:56 of the fourth made it 35-10, and nobody scored again. The 45-point finish kept the Under 50.5 home by 5.5.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Patriots, missed by 23.5 points at the opening Patriots +1.5 and missed by 22.5 points at the closing Patriots +2.5; The Cover Writer, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 3.5 points at the opening 48.5 and fell short by 5.5 points at the closing 50.5.
Called it at both numbers: The Formula, Next Man Up and Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 3.5 points at the opening 48.5 and stayed under by 5.5 points at the closing 50.5.
Follow The Money had no side pick.

Opening line: Giants −1.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: Giants −1.5, over/under 40.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Commanders and the Over, projecting Giants 23, Commanders 22. Final: Commanders 24, Giants 21. The Commanders won by 3, and the teams scored 45 points.

The over/under fell 7 points from the open to the close. Late in the fourth the Giants led 21-17, Letdown Watch's Giants −2.5 was covering, and Follow The Money's Under 41.5 was alive. Then Jordan Stout punted 12 yards out of bounds at 1:54, Deonte Banks was flagged for 33 yards of pass interference, and Jayden Daniels hit Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. Commanders 24, Giants 21, 45 points. The Commanders +2.5 covered by 5.5 for four pickers, Letdown Watch missed by 5.5, and the Over cashed by 3.5 at the card's 41.5 but fell 2.5 short of the opening 47.5.
Missed at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Giants, missed by 4.5 points at the opening Giants −1.5 and missed by 4.5 points at the closing Giants −1.5.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 2.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 4.5 points at the closing 40.5; Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 2.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 4.5 points at the closing 40.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Commanders, covered by 4.5 points at the opening Commanders +1.5 and covered by 4.5 points at the closing Commanders +1.5.
Follow The Money stayed off the side.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: Week 10 is closed. The Cover Writer missed 16 times and hit 12 times at the opening lines, and missed 12 times and hit 16 times at the closing lines, with no pushes.

The Cover Writer finished Week 10 at 9-5 against the spread at both numbers, and 3-11 on the over/under at the open and 7-7 at the close. Monday night went two for two at the card's numbers, the Chargers +4.5 by 7.5 and the Over 38.5 by 4.5. Nine side winners is the most in the room this week. The over/under at the open is a different conversation, and the Munich switch from the Under to the Over is still on the whiteboard.

The Formula finished Week 10 at 8-6 against the spread at both numbers, and 4-10 on the over/under at the open and 8-6 at the close. The Formula broke from the card on Monday night, laid the 4.5 with Baltimore, projected Ravens 25, Chargers 19, and watched the Chargers score 23 and win outright. It cashed the Over and will mention that first. Eight side winners is still a winning week, so it gets to keep its seat at the table.

Next Man Up finished Week 10 at 6-8 against the spread at both numbers, and 5-9 on the over/under at the open and 9-5 at the close. Next Man Up's card named Jacoby Brissett as the Ravens starter, projected Ravens 22, Chargers 21, took the points and the Over, and cashed both. Nobody in the room had a better Monday night. It was 5-8 on the side before that, and the Sunday morning switch off the Seahawks against the Raiders is still the one it would like back.

Letdown Watch finished Week 10 at 8-6 against the spread at both numbers, and 4-10 on the over/under at the open and 8-6 at the close. Letdown Watch had Baltimore at home on 11 days of rest against a team that traveled 2,322 miles, laid the 4.5, and watched the rested home team lose outright. It still has the best side mark in the room since opening-line grading began in Week 8, 24-19 against the spread at the open, and it will bring that up before anybody brings up Monday night.

Follow The Money finished Week 10 at 3-1 against the spread at both numbers, and 8-1 on the over/under at the open and 5-4 at the close. Follow The Money picked four sides all week and cashed three, the Chargers +4.5 on Monday night included. Since Week 8 it is 15-6 on the over/under at the open, the best over/under mark in the room, which it repeats to anybody who will listen and several who won't.

In The Trenches finished Week 10 at 7-7 against the spread at both numbers, and 4-10 on the over/under at the open and 8-6 at the close. In The Trenches projected 39 points on Monday night, took the Over 38.5 and got 43. It cashed the Chargers too. The five Sunday morning over/under switches are still the story of its week. Every call it walked away from would have cashed.

Week 11 starts Thursday at 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video with the Colts at the Texans. The Chargers, now 1-8, host the Jets on Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on Fox, and the four pickers who rode them Monday night get to find out whether one win is a trend.
